title: A raíz de: el origen de un cambio

sections.content: A raíz de (as a result of, stemming from) introduces the event or situation that triggered a later change -- useful for explaining why a policy lost momentum or a program was wound down over time. It's followed by a noun phrase, not a full clause. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: A raíz de estos resultados decepcionantes, el entusiasmo estadounidense por el programa comenzó a disminuir de forma notable.
items.english: As a result of these disappointing results, American enthusiasm for the program began to noticeably decline.

items.spanish: A raíz de la guerra de Vietnam, Washington destinó cada vez menos atención y recursos a los programas de desarrollo en América Latina.
items.english: As a result of the Vietnam War, Washington devoted less and less attention and resources to development programs in Latin America.

items.spanish: A raíz del cambio de administración en 1969, la Alianza para el Progreso perdió gradualmente su identidad propia.
items.english: As a result of the change of administration in 1969, the Alliance for Progress gradually lost its own identity.

items.spanish: A raíz de este final relativamente silencioso, muchos historiadores debaten hoy si el programa cumplió realmente sus metas originales.
items.english: As a result of this relatively quiet end, many historians today debate whether the program actually met its original goals.

sections.content: Don't confuse a raíz de with a causa de -- a raíz de emphasizes that something is the starting point of a chain of consequences, while a causa de simply states a reason. A raíz de works especially well at the start of a sentence about a turning point.
